title: cost-optimization: autounit/batching & caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Natarajan
ci_checks: integration (canary) - failed on first run (timeout in perf-canary), rerun passed
commits: Initial autotune framework and config defaults (authored by priya)
Add quantization profile registry and selection heuristics
Introduce batching & caching default profiles + telemetry hooks
Unit economics CLI tooling and dashboard export (uecon)
Fixed race in runtime batcher and added a metric for cache hit rate
description:
Motivation: Customers commonly overprovision inference capacity because optimal batching, caching, and quantization settings vary by workload. This PR introduces end-to-end automation and tooling to make cost-performance tradeoffs safer and easier for engineering teams.

What this does: consolidates three workstreams into one deliverable: (1) an autotune framework that suggests and applies batching/caching defaults per route, (2) a quantization profile registry and selection heuristic to pick safe quant variants, and (3) unit-economics (uecon) tooling to estimate token-level cost/reliability impact and export metrics to the Console.

Details (single-line description): Adds an autotune runner that collects request histograms and recommends per-route batch_size/latency SLO targets; implements default caching policies that enable prefix+kv caching with safe TTLs; introduces a quantization profile registry with rules mapping model families & sequence distributions -> recommended quant levels; ships a uecon CLI and Prom exporter that computes estimated $/1M tokens and expected tail-latency regressions given a candidate config.

Testing: Unit tests for runner heuristics, integration tests exercising batcher+cache interaction, and a perf-canary validated the end-to-end impact (avg token-cost -17% on sample corpora, p95 latency within SLO for canary routes).

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.autotune.enabled (off by default). We'll enable for internal canary workspace for 48h, monitor uecon metrics and p95 latency, then progressively enable for customers who opt-in. Fallback: runtime will automatically revert to pinned model/config on SLO breach.

Related: ENG-4123 (autotune design), ENG-4189 (uecon dashboards), PM-221 (product acceptance criteria).
